data.name: Lalith
data.long_meaning: Lalitha is a graceful and beautiful goddess in Hindu mythology. She is the consort of Lord Vishnu and is often depicted as a young, beautiful woman. Her name is derived from the Sanskrit word 'lalita', which means 'playful' or 'graceful'. Lalitha is believed to bestow grace, beauty, and prosperity upon her devotees.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbol of divine grace and beauty

vedic_reference.note: Lalitha is a popular name in Hindu mythology and is also the name of a goddess. She is often depicted as a beautiful and graceful goddess who is the embodiment of divine playful energy. In the Vedas, Lalitha is mentioned as a form of the goddess Parvati, the consort of Shiva.

data.cultural_impact: The name Lalitha holds significant cultural importance in Hinduism as it is associated with the revered Hindu goddess Lalitha or Lalita Tripura Sundari, believed to epitomize beauty, grace, and power. She is celebrated as the embodiment of the goddess Saraswati, Laxmi, and Kali combined, and is often depicted as seated on a lotus, surrounded by various deities and attributes. The name Lalitha represents the joy and beauty that is inherent in the divine feminine.
data.spiritual_significance: Lalitha, as a name embodies the spiritual significance of grace and beauty that is interpreted as the manifestation of divinity. The Hindu goddess Lalitha is often invoked to grant blessings of beauty, grace, and wealth while also offering protection against negative energies and obstacles. Lalitha's name is a reminder that the divine is present within each of us and that we can tap into that inner divinity through devotion and faith. Following the name's derivatives from 'lalita', the name Lalitha conveys a sense of playfulness and joy that is echoed in the devotional practices and rituals associated with the goddess.

historical_references.reference: Lalita Sahasranamam is a text in the Mahabharata that lists a thousand names of the Goddess Parvati, and Lalita is one of them. It is believed that chanting these names can bestow blessings and knowledge.
historical_references.context: Mahabharata is an ancient Indian epic that is a major source of Hindu mythology and philosophy. Parvati is the wife of Shiva, one of the principal deities in Hinduism.

historical_references.reference: Another reference to Lalita is found in the Lalita Vistara, a 12th-century Sanskrit text that describes the divine play or leela of the goddess Parvati. In this text, Lalita is depicted as the divine mother and a manifestation of the goddess Saraswati, the goddess of knowledge.
historical_references.context: Sanskrit texts are a rich source of Hindu mythology, philosophy, and literature. The Lalita Vistara is a significant text that provides insights into the divine play or leela of the goddess Parvati.
